correctness.rationale: Convexity and invariance justify reducing every symmetric stochastic matrix with fixed core-core entries to one common cross-edge parameter. The orthogonal subspace decomposition gives eigenvalues 1-sa (m-1), 1-ma-st (s-1), 1-(m+s)a (1). The exact interval of feasible cross-edge parameters for a candidate spectral radius is nonempty iff all seven rational-affine lower bounds hold. Constructing a as its lower endpoint proves attainment, including both parameter boundaries. Independent exact Fraction vertex minimization matched 3332 cases, 180 exact matrix decompositions and 3001 checks of the four-regime witness; the all-real proof is symbolic, not an inference from enumeration.

originality.rationale: The novel object is the exact all-s,m closed-form SLEM envelope with individually prescribed clique-edge transitions. The 2004 SDP formulation is general but does not evaluate this envelope; the 2007 complete-bipartite theorem covers only the t=0 boundary; 2020 clique-lifting optimizes internal clique weights freely, which does not solve a fixed-edge constraint; 2019 friendship-graph frontier has different topology. Searches of research records found no equivalent or dominating constrained split-graph claim. Specialist publication priority remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible mathematical paper might contain the same constrained full split-graph frontier or imply it by a more general explicit parameterized constrained theorem.
The 2004 SDP framework already establishes computability, so the contribution is the all-parameter analytic closed form and four-phase structural specialization, not existence of the convex program.

value.rationale: Prescribed core-edge interactions are a natural external constraint in consensus and reversible network design. The theorem gives a closed-form global constrained SLEM frontier for all complete split graphs and an exact four-stage transition for (s,m)=(5,2): first decreasing, then decreasing at a different rate, then exactly flat, then increasing. The plateau has two distinct rational endpoints 1/10 and 1/6 and does not follow from the known unconstrained optimum. These structural effects, not merely algorithmic reproducibility, motivate the precise invariant.
